pr.title: Store each summary's changed files at the head for the site to serve
pr.head: 377870e6381e5295be513dd8ba3a8d4cceed85b1

summary: A summary page, the guided review page that the Projector site serves at reviews/<number>/, shows each changed file only as its diff hunks: the changed lines plus Git's three lines of context around them. A reader who needs the function a hunk sits in, or the lines between two hunks, has to leave the page for GitHub. The page cannot fetch the file itself, because a private repository's site has no token and the branch may have moved past the summarized head. So the file has to travel with the summary.
This pull request is the data half of the summary-diff-context plan. It changes two steps:

1. Publish stores the head's files. project summary publish already commits summary.json, diff.patch, and attributes.json to summaries/<number>/<head>/ on the hidden ref refs/projector/summaries. It now also adds a head/<path> entry for each changed file whose diff hides lines. Each entry names the blob the head commit already has, so the ref gains tree entries and no new file content.
  2. The site build serves them and computes the gaps. build_summaries checks each stored file against its diff, writes each distinct file once to reviews/blobs/<id>.txt under the site's base, and adds a context entry to the file in the page's data.json that lists the hidden runs of lines, the gaps.

Nothing on the page draws context yet, so pages look the same after this lands. The expander controls are rollout step 2 of the plan, in a later pull request. Landing the data first means every summary published from now on can expand once the page learns how.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Summaries ref: refs/projector/summaries, a hidden ref (not a branch) where publish commits each summary, and which the site deploy checks out.
  • Head file: the head commit's version of a changed file, stored as a tree entry under head/ beside the summary.
  • Gap: a run of head lines that no hunk shows, above the first hunk, between two hunks, or below the last. start and end are new-side line numbers, and oldStart is the old-side number of start.
  • Blob id: the hash Git gives a file's bytes, used to name each served file so two heads with the same content share one file.

groups.title: Publish stores the head's files
groups.kicker: Which changed files publish stores under head/, and how it writes them without new content
intro: When project summary publish commits a summary, it now also lists the head commit's tree and picks the changed files a page could expand. It writes one index entry per file under head/, pointing at the head's existing blob, so publishing adds no file content to the summaries ref.
A file is stored only when all of these hold:

• Its diff has a hunk, so it is text.
  • It is neither new nor deleted, because those diffs already show every line.
  • Its head entry is a regular file (mode 100644 or 100755), not a symlink or a submodule.
  • Its blob is at most CONTEXT_MAX_BYTES, 1 MiB.
  • It is not a .gitattributes file. A stored one would change or drop its neighbors when the deploy checks the ref out or site serve archives it.

Before this change, the code that fetched the head when the checkout lacked it lived inside publish_attributes. It now lives in readable_head, which the attributes and the new head_blobs share, so a publish fetches the head at most once.

checks.text: When the head cannot be read, publish prints one message on stderr and stores neither attributes nor head files. A republish that cannot read the head keeps what an earlier publish stored, because summary_tree starts from the ref's existing tree.

files.note: Adds the head-file listing (head_blobs), the shared head fetch (readable_head), hunk numbers in parse_diff, and the index entries in summary_tree.

checks.text: Each hunk now carries oldStart, oldLines, newStart, and newLines from its @@ header. A side written without a count, such as +12, has one line. The site build uses these numbers to find the gaps without parsing headers again.

git() now reads and writes UTF-8 explicitly and replaces bytes that are not UTF-8. Without that, a path in another encoding in the head's tree would crash the ls-tree listing. Such a path matches no diff path, so it is simply not stored.

The entries are written with update-index -z --index-info as mode 100644 naming the head's blob. The publish test lists the remote's objects before and after and finds only summary.json, diff.patch, and attributes.json new, so the head files add no objects. I ran the suite at this head.

The eligibility rules start here: a hunk, not new, not deleted, and a base name other than .gitattributes. The mode check follows in the ls-tree loop, and the size check uses one cat-file --batch-check call for all candidate blobs.

files.note: Publishes a change to a file of every kind and checks that only the two expandable files get head/ entries, then republishes from a clone that cannot read the head.

checks.text: commit_context_change builds one commit that changes a plain file, an executable, a deleted file, a new file, a file over 1 MiB, a nested .gitattributes, a binary file, a symlink, and a submodule. Only keep.txt and tool.sh should be stored.

groups.title: The site build serves each file once and finds the gaps
groups.kicker: How the deploy checks, writes, and describes each stored head file
intro: For each file on a summary page, build_summaries now looks for that file under the summary's head/ folder. When it finds one, add_context:

1. Decodes it as UTF-8 with replacement and turns each CRLF into LF, because the build reads diff.patch in Python's text mode, which does the same to the diff.
  2. Checks every context and added line of the diff against the stored line with the same number. On a mismatch it drops the file with a ::warning title=Context dropped:: line, so a wrong file never shows wrong lines.
  3. Computes the gaps. A file whose hunks leave no gap gets no context.
  4. Writes the decoded text once to reviews/blobs/<id>.txt, named by the Git blob id of the stored bytes (SHA-256 when the head id has 64 digits), and records {url, lines, gaps} as the file's context.
The build prints how many files it wrote this way and their total size. The pull request body reports that this repository's summaries would produce 289 files, about 10.8 MiB.

checks.text: Anyone who can push the summaries ref also writes the diff that names each path, so the build must never let a path read outside head/. stored_head_file enforces that.

files.note: Adds stored_head_file, shows_diff, hunk_gaps, blob_id, and add_context, and calls add_context for every built summary.

checks.text: The joined path is resolved and must stay under the summary's head/ folder, so .., an absolute path from the diff, and a symlink that leads out all read nothing. A symlinked <number>/<head> folder also reads nothing, since its resolved target never lies under the unresolved folder. test_a_path_that_leads_out_of_the_head_folder_reads_nothing covers .. and a symlink.

A hunk with no lines on a side sits after its start line, hence the + 1 when the count is 0. I ran add_context on this pull request's own diff of this file and of summary.py, against their head copies, and every gap matched the hunk headers.
The served text is the CRLF-normalized decode, but the file is named by the id of the raw stored bytes, so the name still traces back to the Git object.

files.note: HunkGapTests pins the gap arithmetic at the edges, and ContextBuildTests builds a site with base /projector/ and checks the served files, the URL, the mismatch warning, and the path guard.
